manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Australian waterbirds cannot be treated as a simple static SDM problem; many taxa track pulsed, spatially shifting wetlands.
best_supporting_sources: Kingsford & Norman 2002; Roshier et al. 2001; Kingsford et al. 2010; Teitelbaum & Mueller 2019; Abrahms et al. 2021.
gaps_or_cautions: Do not infer individual movement from occurrence data alone; use tracking papers and structured surveys for movement claims.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Hydrological predictors should include current wetness, antecedent wetness, hydroperiod/persistence, drying stage or velocity, and re-wetting/event novelty.
best_supporting_sources: Mueller et al. 2016; Roshier et al. 2001; Yang et al. 2008; Cumming et al. 2021; Arthur et al. 2012; Dunn et al. 2023.
evidence_strength: Strong for wetness/persistence; moderate for novelty
gaps_or_cautions: 'Novelty' must be operationally defined as contrast from recent/local hydrological history, not assumed to be perceived novelty.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Regional water availability matters: a wetland's attractiveness depends on what is available elsewhere.
best_supporting_sources: Roshier et al. 2001; Wen et al. 2016; Bino et al. 2020; Nicol et al. 2024; McGinness et al. 2024 inland-flyway paper.
gaps_or_cautions: Regional scarcity is an analyst-defined landscape context; do not imply birds know the full regional water map.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Breeding response should be separated from occurrence and abundance.
best_supporting_sources: Arthur et al. 2012; Bino et al. 2014; Kingsford & Auld 2005; Pedler et al. 2018; Brandis et al. 2024; McGinness et al. 2025.
gaps_or_cautions: Breeding initiation, nest persistence, fledging, and recruitment are different endpoints; citizen observations rarely measure all.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Open-water remote sensing is powerful but incomplete habitat measurement.
best_supporting_sources: Mueller et al. 2016; Krause et al. 2021; Dunn et al. 2023; DEA Waterbodies v3.0; Brandis et al. 2024.
gaps_or_cautions: Vegetated wetlands, under-canopy water, water depth, salinity, turbidity, and nesting substrate may be missed or poorly represented.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: DEA Waterbodies is appropriate for persistent open-water units but not all wetland habitat.
best_supporting_sources: Krause et al. 2021; DEA Waterbodies v3.0; Dunn et al. 2023.
gaps_or_cautions: The product estimates wet surface area; it explicitly does not provide depth, volume, water source, or ecological quality.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Citizen-science observations require effort, protocol, detectability, and sampling-bias covariates.
best_supporting_sources: Hochachka et al. 2023; Johnston et al. 2020; Bird et al. 2014; Callaghan et al. 2021; Backstrom et al. 2025.
gaps_or_cautions: Complete checklists are more defensible than incidental records; ALA/Birdata records may be mixed-protocol.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: EAWS is suitable for independent validation and/or data integration, not as flawless ground truth.
best_supporting_sources: Kingsford et al. 2020; Caley et al. 2022; Adde et al. 2021.
gaps_or_cautions: Aerial surveys have their own spatial design, visibility, timing, and count-error structure.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Integrated distribution models are justified for combining eBird/Birdata/ALA with aerial surveys.
best_supporting_sources: Miller et al. 2019; Adde et al. 2021; Dorazio 2014; Tobler et al. 2019.
gaps_or_cautions: The integration model must state which latent ecological process each data stream informs.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Dynamic occupancy/count models are preferable to a static presence-only SDM for this problem.
best_supporting_sources: MacKenzie et al. 2003; Dail & Madsen 2011; Kéry & Royle Vol. 2; Caley et al. 2022.
gaps_or_cautions: Occupancy may be biologically thin for flocks; counts or intensity models may be needed for abundance/aggregation.

best_supporting_sources: Bino et al. 2020; Becker et al. 2024; McGinness et al. 2024 mixed-strategy paper; Tobler et al. 2019; Pedersen et al. 2019.
gaps_or_cautions: Guilds should be ecological hypotheses, not arbitrary convenience groups.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: Validation should use spatial, temporal, and environmental/hydrological-event blocking.
best_supporting_sources: Roberts et al. 2017; Valavi et al. 2019; Hijmans 2012; Fourcade et al. 2014; Backstrom et al. 2025.
gaps_or_cautions: Event-blocking is a logical extension; it must be clearly defined and reported.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: 'Hydrological reaction norm' is a useful framing if explicitly defined as an estimated response surface.
best_supporting_sources: Dingemanse & Wolf 2010; Wood 2017; Pedersen et al. 2019; Abrahms et al. 2021.
gaps_or_cautions: Do not imply genetic reaction norms or individual plasticity unless individual-level longitudinal data exist.

manuscript_claim_or_design_decision: False refugia/ecological traps should be hypotheses, not assumed conclusions.
best_supporting_sources: Schlaepfer et al. 2002; Robertson & Hutto 2006; Vander Vorste et al. 2020; Bino et al. 2015.
gaps_or_cautions: A trap claim requires preference/attraction plus lower fitness or demographic cost.
